question: What is the main job of a mechanical ventilator in the hospital ward?

options.A: To support or replace spontaneous breathing
options.B: To permanently eliminate the need for oxygen therapy
options.C: To cure underlying pulmonary infections
options.D: To lower systemic blood pressure safely

explanation: Think of the ventilator as an extra pair of lungs for patients who are too tired or sick to breathe well on their own. It takes over or helps out until they recover!

question: What do we call the spread of cancer cells to other parts of the body?

options.A: Carcinogenesis
options.B: Metastasis
options.C: Hyperplasia
options.D: Apoptosis

explanation: Fantastic! Metastasis is when cancer cells break away from the main tumor, travel through the body, and set up secondary tumor camps elsewhere.

question: Why is potassium iodide used less often than guaifenesin as an expectorant?

options.A: It turns respiratory secretions completely solid instead of thinning them
options.B: It requires careful monitoring due to potential effects on the thyroid gland
options.C: It can only be administered through direct injection into the bone marrow
options.D: It completely stops all patient movement and causes heavy sedation

explanation: Spot on. Because iodide can mess with the thyroid gland if used for too long, nurses prefer safer options like guaifenesin.

question: A patient on chemotherapy calls the clinic saying their temperature is 38.5°C. What should you tell them to do?

options.A: Drink plenty of cold fluids and monitor the temperature for another day.
options.B: Apply a cool damp cloth to the forehead to bring down the fever.
options.C: Take a dose of paracetamol and rest in bed until tomorrow morning.
options.D: Come to the hospital immediately for a medical evaluation and blood work.

explanation: Fever in a chemo patient is an emergency because their immune system is low. Quick action can save a life!

question: You just passed your board exams and submitted your papers. What do you still need before you can legally start working on the ward?

options.A: Receiving the official practicing license certificate or registration number
options.B: Completing a mandatory five-year tenure in a rural health center
options.C: Obtaining written permission from the local community development association
options.D: Purchasing personal medical diagnostic equipment for the hospital

explanation: Passing the exam is a huge relief! But you must wait to physically or digitally have your license number before you can independently care for patients.

question: What is the standard formula used to calculate Body Mass Index (BMI)?

options.A: Weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared
options.B: Height in meters divided by weight in pounds squared
options.C: Weight in pounds multiplied by height in inches
options.D: Height in centimeters divided by weight in kilograms

explanation: You got it! Weight in kg divided by height in meters squared ($kg/m^2$) is the classic formula you will use all through your nursing practice.

question: What is the typical acid-base blood gas state during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: Acute metabolic alkalosis
options.B: Uncompensated metabolic acidosis
options.C: Severe respiratory acidosis
options.D: Compensated respiratory alkalosis

explanation: Mums breathe off extra carbon dioxide, leading to mild respiratory alkalosis which the kidneys smoothly balance out with bicarbonate. Great revision!

question: Where does a prohormone usually get turned into its final, active hormone form?

options.A: Inside secretory vesicles as they wait to be released
options.B: Directly on the surface of the rough endoplasmic reticulum
options.C: Inside the cell nucleus during the transcription of DNA
options.D: Out in the bloodstream after the molecule leaves the cell

explanation: The final cutting and polishing happens right inside the storage bubbles (secretory vesicles) as the cell waits for the signal to release the hormone.

question: A student is found to have a severe heart murmur during a routine school check. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.A: Ignore the finding since the child looks healthy
options.B: Refer the student to a specialized pediatric clinic
options.C: Instruct the class teacher to prescribe medication
options.D: Send the child home permanently from school

explanation: Serious conditions detected during school screenings require formal referral to medical specialists for proper diagnosis and management. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h2)

question: Around the sixth day after delivery, what kind of vaginal discharge is most normal to see?

options.A: Bright red clots
options.B: Clear watery fluid
options.C: Pinkish-brown discharge
options.D: Yellowish-white creamy discharge

explanation: Brilliant! As healing continues, lochia changes from red to a thinner, pinkish-brown fluid called lochia serosa around days five through nine.

question: A nurse is managing a patient with severe dehydration using a standing order, but the patient suddenly becomes lethargic and stops responding. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Send the patient home with instructions to drink more water tomorrow
options.B: Stabilize emergency airway and breathing, write a referral note, and arrange transfer
options.C: Discard the standing order book and close the clinic for the day
options.D: Increase the oral rehydration fluid volume and wait another two hours

explanation: Deterioration requires stopping routine care, stabilizing urgent life threats, and transferring the patient to a higher facility. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h8)

question: What skill must a good nursing leader have alongside management abilities?

options.A: Political party affiliation
options.B: Strong clinical acumen
options.C: Advanced legal training
options.D: Full financial control

explanation: To earn the respect of the nursing team, a leader needs to understand real bedside care and know current clinical guidelines inside and out.

question: Why is a silent chest in a patient with severe asthma considered a dangerous emergency?

options.A: It means air is no longer moving in or out of the lungs
options.B: It is a normal finding during deep sleep
options.C: It shows that the inhaler medication worked successfully
options.D: It indicates the asthma attack has completely resolved

explanation: A silent chest means the airways are so tight or blocked that air cannot move at all, which signals immediate respiratory arrest. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the main goal of an electrophysiologic study (EPS)?

options.A: To clear blocked plaque from the coronary arteries
options.B: To measure the exact volume of blood pumped per minute
options.C: To record surface electrical signals without touching the heart
options.D: To map the electrical system of the heart from the inside

explanation: Think of an EPS as an electrical wiring check! Special tiny wires (catheters) are put right inside the heart chambers to see how the electrical signals are flowing. You've got this!

question: A patient has a fresh bacterial infection. Which white blood cell is usually the very first responder on the scene?

options.A: Neutrophil
options.B: Platelet
options.C: Erythrocyte
options.D: Albumin

explanation: Neutrophils are the heavy-duty first responders of the cellular world! They rush immediately to acute bacterial infections to gobble up and destroy the invaders.

question: A patient with a tracheostomy suddenly struggles to breathe, turns bluish, and you can't pass a suction catheter down the tube. What is likely happening?

options.A: Normal post-operative recovery
options.B: A mucous plug blocking the airway
options.C: The cuff is completely deflated
options.D: The oxygen flow rate is too high

explanation: If your catheter won't go through and the patient is in distress, a thick mucous plug is usually blocking the pipe. This is an urgent call for action!

question: A child's weight-for-length falls way below the minus two Z-score on the growth chart. What does this mean?

options.A: Advanced neurological maturity
options.B: Chronic skeletal stunting
options.C: Acute malnutrition or wasting
options.D: Normal developmental variation

explanation: You're doing great! Weight-for-length compares mass to height. A very low score means the child has recently lost weight and is too thin for their height—a sign of wasting.

question: Which leadership approach is most likely to crush motivation among clinical nursing staff?

options.A: Transparent communication and fair workload distribution
options.B: Actively listening to concerns before making decisions
options.C: Micromanagement and shifting blame onto subordinates
options.D: Providing constructive feedback during regular evaluations

explanation: Nobody likes a boss who breathes down their neck and always blames others. Trust and teamwork build great nurses instead!

question: What is the primary purpose of therapeutic hypothermia in a newborn who experienced severe distress?

options.A: To help the baby breathe room air without support
options.B: To speed up the healing of meconium-stained skin
options.C: To reduce ongoing brain injury and cell death
options.D: To lower the baby's risk of developing infant jaundice

explanation: Cooling the baby's body temperature slows down damaging chemical reactions in the brain after a severe lack of oxygen. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h7)

question: What do we mean by "illness behaviour"?

options.A: The laboratory test results confirming an infection
options.B: The permanent physical damage caused by a disease
options.C: How a doctor chooses the correct medication dosage
options.D: How a person responds to symptoms and seeks help

explanation: Think of illness behaviour as the steps people take when something feels off in their body—ranging from staying home to rest, to visiting the clinic for help. You've got this!

question: What does 'participatory governance' mean in primary health care?

options.A: Leaving all health decisions entirely to elected politicians
options.B: Allowing only doctors to vote on clinic budgets
options.C: Involving local community members in health planning and decisions
options.D: Handing over total hospital ownership to private investors

explanation: Spot on! Participatory governance means the community isn't just a receiver of care—they help shape the health services they get. Keep up the great work!

question: What are the finger-like projections of the fallopian tube that catch the released egg called?

options.A: Villi
options.B: Stigma
options.C: Cilia
options.D: Fimbriae

explanation: The fimbriae wave gently over the ovary like little fingers, ready to sweep the newly released egg safely into the fallopian tube.

question: What is the earliest physical sign of puberty in boys?

options.A: A sudden linear height spurt
options.B: Growth of facial hair
options.C: Deepening of the voice
options.D: Enlargement of the testes

explanation: Spot on! Testicular growth is the very first clinical sign that male puberty has begun.

question: How do modern informatics tools make communication between different healthcare pros much easier?

options.A: By providing a centralized digital hub for notes, labs, and orders
options.B: By allowing patients to directly alter their medication schedules
options.C: By automatically calling doctors whenever a vital sign changes
options.D: By replacing all face-to-face shift change meetings entirely

explanation: Spot on! Having one central digital chart means doctors, nurses, and pharmacists are all looking at the exact same page, reducing miscommunication on the ward.

question: Why does Staphylococcus food poisoning cause sudden vomiting very soon after eating?

options.A: It blocks normal movement in the large intestine
options.B: It destroys the stomach lining with acid
options.C: It produces toxins in the food before you even eat it
options.D: It multiplies inside the bloodstream instantly

explanation: Think of Staph as leaving nasty toxins behind in food left out too long. Once you eat it, those pre-made toxins trigger rapid vomiting. Makes total sense, right?

question: A nursing student in a sterile gown accidentally lets their hands drop below their waist. What should they do?

options.A: Step back one foot and continue assisting the surgeon
options.B: Continue working because the gown is still clean on top
options.C: Acknowledge that sterility is broken and get a new gown
options.D: Ask the circulating nurse to wipe the gloves with alcohol

explanation: In theatre rules, anything below the waist is considered unsterile. Don't worry—accidents happen! Just step back, re-gown, and keep learning.

question: As a nurse, what is one of the best ways you can help stop drug resistance?

options.A: Administering broad-spectrum drugs for every common viral cold
options.B: Educating patients to finish their entire antibiotic prescription
options.C: Stopping medication immediately once mild symptoms disappear
options.D: Encouraging patients to save leftover pills for future sickness

explanation: You got it! Always remind patients to complete their meds. Stopping early leaves the toughest germs alive to breed stronger, resistant generations.

question: Which graph is better than a pie chart for tracking patient recovery over several months?

options.A: A pie chart
options.B: A line graph
options.C: A raw data list
options.D: A frequency table

explanation: You got it! Line graphs are your best friend for showing changes and trends over time.

question: Why is it so important to set rehabilitation goals together with the patient?

options.A: Patients usually know more about pharmacology than doctors do
options.B: Hospital policies legally forbid nurses from writing goals alone
options.C: Goals matter more and motivate the patient when they reflect personal values
options.D: Collaborative goals take less time to write out in charts

explanation: When patients help choose their goals, they feel heard and stay much more motivated to work hard during therapy!

question: Why must a feeding tube be flushed with warm water before and after giving formula?

options.A: To check the patient's blood pressure
options.B: To prevent the tube from clogging
options.C: To hydrate the patient's skin
options.D: To cool down the internal stomach lining

explanation: You got it! Flushing clears out thick formula or crushed meds so the narrow tube doesn't block up.

question: Which rehab team member helps patients master everyday tasks like eating, bathing, and dressing?

options.A: Physiatrist
options.B: Physical therapist
options.C: Occupational therapist
options.D: Speech-language pathologist

explanation: Occupational therapists (OTs) are the masters of 'occupations'—meaning everyday living activities. They help patients get back to doing things for themselves!

question: How does severe kidney disease affect how medications act in the body?

options.A: It immediately destroys the drug inside the stomach.
options.B: It prevents the drug from ever entering the bloodstream.
options.C: It delays drug clearance and causes dangerous accumulation.
options.D: It turns all medications into inactive sugar compounds.

explanation: Since the kidneys act like the body's filter, disease makes it hard for them to clear out drugs. This causes the medicine to pile up to unsafe levels.

question: Why are interdisciplinary rounds (where different health workers meet together) so helpful?

options.A: They ensure that doctors make all decisions without input from nurses
options.B: They allow multiple departments to discuss care plans together in real time
options.C: They remove the need for any documentation in the patient chart
options.D: They replace the nursing management team with administrative staff

explanation: Brilliant! Bringing everyone together at once clears up confusion instantly so the whole healthcare team is on the exact same page for the patient.

question: Which parasite forms tough outer shells (cysts) that survive normal chlorine treatment in water?

options.A: Giardia lamblia
options.B: Streptococcus pneumoniae
options.C: Staphylococcus aureus
options.D: Plasmodium falciparum

explanation: Giardia is a stubborn protozoan that builds protective cysts. These cysts help it survive tough conditions and shrug off standard amounts of chlorine in water treatment.

question: Which medication is standard for stopping seizures in a pregnant woman with eclampsia?

options.A: Sodium bicarbonate
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Calcium gluconate
options.D: Diazepam drops

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is the magic word here! It is the go-to drug to control and prevent seizures in eclampsia.

question: Why do clinicians frequently order a skin biopsy for stubborn rashes?

options.A: To stretch tight scar tissue and improve the overall range of motion
options.B: To drain large amounts of purulent fluid from a deep subcutaneous abscess
options.C: To examine tissue architecture under a microscope for a definitive diagnosis
options.D: To permanently numb the surrounding nerve endings and stop chronic itching

explanation: Exactly! Taking a tiny tissue sample lets the lab look closely at the cell structure to figure out the exact cause of the rash.

question: What is the main job of promoting agents during the second stage of cancer?

options.A: To help the immune system destroy early cancer cells
options.B: To stimulate previously mutated cells to divide and multiply
options.C: To stop blood vessels from growing into the tumor
options.D: To cause the initial DNA damage inside the cell nucleus

explanation: Correct! Promoters don't start the mutation themselves, but they act like fertilizer, encouraging those already-mutated cells to multiply and grow.

question: How can market-driven hospital policies directly impact bedside nursing practice?

options.A: By prioritizing fast patient turnover and tight staffing ratios
options.B: By eliminating all administrative paperwork duties
options.C: By ensuring nurses control hospital budgets
options.D: By guaranteeing unlimited time for patient education

explanation: Corporate models focus on efficiency and cost reduction, which often translates to leaner staffing and faster discharges. [learn more](GST322_U1_T4#GST322_U1_T4_h6)

question: What does interoperability mean in healthcare technology?

options.A: Patients can update their own charts without a clinician
options.B: Every hospital uses a completely different brand of computer
options.C: Doctors and nurses work separate shifts without communicating
options.D: Different health systems can share data seamlessly

explanation: Interoperability allows separate computer networks and hospitals to talk to each other and exchange patient records safely. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h2)

question: A patient had a deep cut on their shin stitched 8 days ago and asks to remove the stitches. What do you tell them?

options.A: Yes, because leg wounds heal faster than any other body part
options.B: Yes, all sutures can safely come out after exactly seven days
options.C: No, sutures must stay in place for at least a full month
options.D: No, limb and joint wounds usually need ten to fourteen days of healing support

explanation: Areas over joints or shins move a lot and have less blood flow, so they need 10 to 14 days before taking stitches out. Safety first!

question: What is the main goal of doing a hysterosalpingography test during an infertility workup?

options.A: To count the total number of immature eggs remaining in the ovaries
options.B: To check the thyroid gland for signs of overactivity
options.C: To visualize the uterine cavity and check if fallopian tubes are open
options.D: To measure the exact daily progesterone levels in the blood

explanation: Awesome job! During this test, dye is put through the cervix so x-rays can show if the fluid flows nicely through the tubes. You're building solid practical knowledge!

question: Why shouldn't a nurse rely *only* on the p-value when deciding to change how patients are cared for?

options.A: Hospital administrators only look at qualitative nurse interviews
options.B: Journal articles often hide the actual t-statistic value
options.C: P-values cannot be trusted when sample sizes are large
options.D: Statistical significance does not guarantee meaningful clinical impact

explanation: Just because a finding is statistically 'real' doesn't mean it makes a big enough difference to change everyday bedside nursing practice. Always look at the clinical picture!

question: What is a major environmental risk factor that can push someone toward substance abuse?

options.A: Living in a house with too many windows
options.B: Having a naturally slow resting heart rate
options.C: Eating a diet low in essential vitamins
options.D: Peer pressure and easy availability of drugs

explanation: That's right! Surroundings matter a lot. Hanging out with peers who use drugs and having easy access makes it much harder to say no.

question: Up to what gestational age is MVA typically performed in the first trimester?

options.A: 28 to 30 weeks
options.B: 12 to 14 weeks
options.C: 4 to 6 weeks
options.D: 20 to 22 weeks

explanation: MVA is designed and validated as a safe and effective procedure for early pregnancy loss and termination up to 12 to 14 weeks of gestation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h1)

question: What is a key visual difference between a bar chart and a histogram?

options.A: Histograms have touching bars because data is continuous
options.B: Histograms are only used for nominal data categories
options.C: Bar charts display changes over time on the vertical axis
options.D: Bar charts use circles instead of rectangular bars

explanation: Because histograms represent continuous numerical ranges, their bars touch each other to show that the scale flows without gaps. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h6)

question: How are the large circumvallate papillae arranged on the human tongue?

options.A: Evenly scattered across the entire ventral surface
options.B: A V-shaped row just anterior to the sulcus terminalis
options.C: Parallel folds exclusively along the posterior edges
options.D: A tight cluster strictly at the very tip of the tongue

explanation: Great job! These big vallate papillae form a neat V-shape right in front of the sulcus terminalis near the back of the tongue.

question: Why is it so important to plan care goals together with the client and their family?

options.A: To shift all legal responsibility for treatment onto the family
options.B: Because care happens in their personal space and must fit their daily reality
options.C: Because hospital rules legally apply to all home settings
options.D: To make sure the nurse does not have to do any heavy lifting

explanation: You got it! As nurses visiting someone's home, our plan has to make sense for their everyday life, or it simply won't work.

question: What is a common trap students fall into when choosing a theory for their project?

options.A: Selecting a framework that is too simple and practical
options.B: Choosing a famous theory that does not actually fit their research topic
options.C: Consulting too many experienced nursing professors for advice
options.D: Reading original texts written by nursing theorists

explanation: True! Sometimes we pick a theory just because it is popular, even if it has nothing to do with our actual study topic.

question: How does desmopressin help patients with mild haemophilia A or von Willebrand disease?

options.A: It replaces vitamin K stores directly in the liver.
options.B: It destroys abnormal platelets in the bloodstream.
options.C: It stimulates the release of stored clotting factors from vessel walls.
options.D: It dissolves dangerous clots blocking major blood vessels.

explanation: Desmopressin gives the body a helpful nudge, telling the blood vessels to release extra stored clotting factors so the blood can clot better.

question: How can community health nurses best fight social stigma against disability?

options.A: By ignoring cultural beliefs entirely without discussion
options.B: By focusing solely on medication management in clinics
options.C: Through patient advocacy and public health education
options.D: By keeping affected individuals hidden safely at home

explanation: Brilliant! Education and speaking up help clear away harmful myths, replacing fear with inclusion and understanding.

question: Which of these behaviors counts as psychological or emotional violence under the VAPP Act?

options.A: Constant intimidation and stalking
options.B: Forgetting to buy household groceries
options.C: Accidental physical injury from sports
options.D: Failing a school promotion examination

explanation: Correct! Mental torture, constant threats, intimidation, and stalking are all forms of psychological abuse covered by the law.

question: Why is clear and prompt documentation of vital signs especially important in a busy Nigerian ward?

options.A: It guarantees that the patient will be discharged early
options.B: It ensures safe continuity of care when shifts change
options.C: It replaces the need to give a verbal handover report
options.D: It prevents patients from asking questions about treatment

explanation: Accurate written records give incoming nursing staff reliable information to safely monitor patients without missing critical changes. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is an outbreak of cholera classified as a biological risk?

options.A: It is caused by living infectious agents spreading through a population
options.B: It only happens because of poor political leadership in the area
options.C: It arises purely from toxic factory smoke polluting the air
options.D: It is a social custom passed down from older generations

explanation: You got it! 'Biological' means living organisms—in this case, bacteria like Vibrio cholerae spreading through water or food.

question: When someone pushes back against your advocacy campaign, which of these should you NOT do?

options.A: Dismissing the critic's concerns as foolish and uneducated
options.B: Anticipating counter-arguments ahead of time with solid data
options.C: Acknowledging their point of view respectfully before pivoting
options.D: Remaining calm, professional, and prepared with evidence

explanation: Never insult or dismiss your critics! Staying respectful keeps your credibility high, even when people disagree with you.

question: Why is it a bad idea to recap needles after giving an injection?

options.A: Government policy requires throwing away the entire syringe un-capped
options.B: It is a leading cause of accidental needle-stick injuries
options.C: It makes the needle sterile again by accident
options.D: It causes the syringe plunger to stick permanently

explanation: Trying to guide a needle back into its cap often leads to accidental finger pricks. It's safer to drop it straight into the box!

question: How do the autonomic and somatic nervous systems team up to keep you continent?

options.A: Somatic nerves open the bladder neck while autonomic nerves squeeze the outer muscles.
options.B: Autonomic fibers manage involuntary internal muscle tone while somatic fibers control the voluntary outer sphincter.
options.C: Both systems rely entirely on conscious thought to prevent accidental leakage.
options.D: Autonomic nerves stop urine production while somatic nerves pump urine down the tube.

explanation: Brilliant! It's a teamwork effort: involuntary nerves handle the inside muscles automatically, while voluntary nerves let you decide when to use the restroom.

question: What is the main advantage of creating a weekly meal plan?

options.A: It stops impulsive buying and reduces food expenses
options.B: It ensures all family members eat the exact same food portions
options.C: It eliminates the need to ever visit a local open-air market
options.D: It guarantees that weight loss will occur within seven days

explanation: That's right! Having a clear plan stops those random, hunger-driven shopping trips that cost way more than expected.

question: Which physical factor is most essential for keeping waterborne diseases out of a neighborhood?

options.A: Multistory housing units with elevators
options.B: Wide concrete roads for vehicle traffic
options.C: Large recreational parks with green spaces
options.D: Consistent access to safe, clean drinking water

explanation: Spot on! Clean water is our absolute best shield against nasty bugs like cholera and typhoid.

question: Why do nurses need to pay attention to the specific 'strain' of a germ listed in a lab report?

options.A: Different strains within the same species can cause vastly different disease severity
options.B: The strain name tells the nurse which commercial disinfectant to spray
options.C: Only specific strains require nurses to document vital signs hourly
options.D: Strains dictate the exact room temperature required for patient isolation

explanation: Even within the same family of germs, one strain might be harmless while another causes severe illness. Knowing the strain helps you anticipate how sick your patient might get.

question: When do you check the Apgar score for a newborn baby?

options.A: At birth and every ten minutes
options.B: At one and five minutes after birth
options.C: At thirty minutes and one hour
options.D: At five and fifteen minutes after birth

explanation: You got this! We check the Apgar score right at 1 minute and 5 minutes of life. This helps us see how well the baby is adjusting to breathing on their own outside the womb.

question: What is one of the best things a community health nurse can do to fight gender bias?

options.A: Forcing patients to abandon their cultural beliefs
options.B: Reporting every community member to the police
options.C: Limiting health education to male household heads
options.D: Providing respectful, judgment-free care to all patients

explanation: Creating a safe, welcoming clinic space where everyone feels respected is a powerful nursing action against discrimination. Keep it up!

question: What happens during a prescribing cascade?

options.A: The pharmacy runs out of basic supplies and substitutes vitamins
options.B: A drug side effect is mistaken for a new illness and treated with another drug
options.C: All medications are washed out of the patient's system at once
options.D: A nurse stops all prescriptions due to a sudden power outage

explanation: The prescribing cascade creates a dangerous cycle where side effects lead to more prescriptions instead of drug discontinuation. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h3)

question: A pregnant patient is struggling with morning sickness and finds it hard to eat three big meals. What is the best advice?

options.A: Force yourself to eat large plates of heavy food to keep your strength up
options.B: Eat small, frequent snacks throughout the day to keep something in the stomach
options.C: Drink strong coffee on an empty stomach to wake up your digestive tract
options.D: Stop drinking all fluids completely until the vomiting stops entirely

explanation: An empty stomach can actually make nausea worse! Nibbling on small, light snacks often helps keep the tummy settled.

question: What is the main downside of using benzodiazepines for a long-term fix for anxiety?

options.A: Severe worsening of depressive symptoms within minutes
options.B: Immediate and permanent liver failure after one dose
options.C: Total lack of effectiveness for acute panic attacks
options.D: Risk of tolerance, dependence, and physical withdrawal

explanation: Benzodiazepines work fast, but they are habit-forming. Over time, the body gets used to them, leading to dependence and tough withdrawal if stopped suddenly.

question: Why is peer support so encouraging for someone newly diagnosed with a permanent physical disability?

options.A: It prevents family members from interfering in treatment decisions
options.B: It replaces the need for professional nursing care and medications
options.C: It connects them with someone who truly understands their lived experience
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will regain full physical movement

explanation: Nothing beats talking to someone who has walked in your shoes. Peer mentors offer real hope and practical tips that textbooks just can't match.

question: How do correlational studies usually help prepare for future clinical trials?

options.A: By replacing the need for any human participants in the lab
options.B: By proving beyond doubt that a treatment cures a disease
options.C: By showing that a relationship exists to justify further research
options.D: By randomly assigning patients to control and treatment groups

explanation: Brilliant! Finding a solid connection in a correlational study gives scientists the green light to invest time and money into bigger experiments.

question: In healthcare, what do we mean by 'information asymmetry'?

options.A: Pharmacies hide drug prices from the public
options.B: Government agencies control all hospital budgets
options.C: Patients and doctors share the exact same level of medical knowledge
options.D: Healthcare providers have deep medical training while patients know very little

explanation: You got it! It simply describes the knowledge gap: doctors and nurses spent years studying medicine, while patients usually rely on them to explain what is wrong.

question: Why can't high-dose iodine solutions be used as a long-term treatment for hyperthyroidism?

options.A: The liver breaks down the iodine molecules before they reach the neck
options.B: Patients rapidly develop severe lifelong addiction to the taste of iodine
options.C: The thyroid gland escapes from the blocking effect after 10 to 14 days
options.D: Prolonged use permanently stains the teeth and oral mucous membranes

explanation: The thyroid is clever—it adjusts to the high iodine levels quickly, meaning the blocking effect wears off in about two weeks.

question: An elderly patient takes a bedtime sedative. What is a key safety point for the nurse to plan for?

options.A: Restricting all fluid intake for twelve hours prior to taking the medication
options.B: Checking blood glucose levels every two hours throughout the night
options.C: Implementing strict fall precautions due to morning dizziness and slowed reflexes
options.D: Encouraging immediate morning jogging to clear the drug from the bloodstream

explanation: Older adults process these drugs more slowly, leading to morning grogginess and an increased risk of nasty slips and falls. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T2#GNS223_U6_T2_h5)

question: Why is it best to kick off a research interview with a gentle, friendly icebreaker?

options.A: To test if the audio recorder is working properly
options.B: To help build trust and put the participant at ease
options.C: To quickly finish the interview before shift change
options.D: To trick the participant into sharing secrets

explanation: Exactly! Hospital studies can feel intimidating to patients. A warm, easy start helps them relax and feel safe with you.

question: Why might a statistically significant result still not be enough to change everyday nursing practice?

options.A: Nurses are not legally allowed to read research papers.
options.B: P-values only tell you about sample size, not patient outcomes.
options.C: A statistically significant result may not be clinically meaningful for patients.
options.D: Statistical tests are always biased toward large hospital systems.

explanation: Spot on! Just because a number is statistically fancy doesn't mean it actually makes a noticeable, helpful difference in a real patient's life.

question: A patient says they take a blood pressure pill every morning. What crucial detail is still missing?

options.A: The name of the pharmacy that sold it
options.B: The color of the box the pills come in
options.C: The exact dosage strength of the pill
options.D: The weather on the day they started it

explanation: Knowing the drug name is good, but without the specific dose, you cannot assess safety or give correct care. You are thinking like a real nurse!

question: What is the popular name of the form Nigerian health workers use to report suspected bad drug reactions?

options.A: The Red Hazard Card
options.B: The Green Incident Sheet
options.C: The Yellow Form
options.D: The Blue Prescription Pad

explanation: You nailed it! The Yellow Form is our trusty go-to paper tool in Nigerian hospitals for reporting suspected drug side effects.

question: Why must nurses weave therapy principles into everyday nursing care?

options.A: To ensure consistent practice and reinforce progress across all shifts
options.B: To shorten the length of the patient's hospital stay
options.C: To replace the physical therapist entirely during night shifts
options.D: To reduce the number of medical documents in the chart

explanation: You got it! Consistency helps patients rebuild their neural pathways and physical strength much faster when practiced all day long.

question: As a nurse, how must you make sure the traction weights are positioned during your shift?

options.A: They are adjusted upward by the patient
options.B: They are hidden beneath heavy wool blankets
options.C: They rest securely on the foot of the bed
options.D: They hang freely without touching the floor

explanation: Always check those weights! If they touch the floor, they lose their pulling power and the therapy won't work.

question: What is the primary goal of Adolescent and Youth-Friendly Health Services?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on the treatment of geriatric illnesses
options.B: Banning teenagers from visiting local community pharmacies
options.C: Providing confidential and accessible care without judgment
options.D: Requiring parental consent for every routine consultation

explanation: That's right! Youth-friendly centers remove barriers like judgmental attitudes and lack of privacy so young people feel safe seeking help.

question: Which of these is a key safety outcome indicator in a hospital setting?

options.A: Rate of patient falls with injury
options.B: Total number of staff on annual leave
options.C: Number of visiting family members per day
options.D: Cost of purchasing new intravenous pumps

explanation: Patient falls with injury tell us directly how well our safety measures are protecting vulnerable patients on the ward.

question: Why do specialty nurses, like nurse anesthetists, pay higher malpractice insurance rates?

options.A: They are legally required to own three separate insurance policies at the same time
options.B: Hospital administrators force specialty nurses to subsidize general floor coverage
options.C: Insurance companies charge extra fees for nurses who work night shifts
options.D: Their specialized clinical roles carry a statistically higher risk of severe patient complications

explanation: Higher risk areas deal with critical life-and-death procedures where a small mistake can have massive consequences, so insurance costs more.

question: A nurse manager wants to know if staff truly feel safe reporting errors. What is the best way to get honest feedback?

options.A: Reviewing personal patient care notes written by individual staff nurses
options.B: Conducting mandatory public interviews with the entire nursing unit
options.C: Administering anonymous written or digital surveys about workplace safety
options.D: Asking physicians to report on the performance of junior nurses

explanation: Great choice! Anonymity gives staff the psychological safety to speak their minds without stressing about getting into trouble.

question: What causes the chemical imbalances known as Tumor Lysis Syndrome?

options.A: Eating too many potassium-rich foods during chemo
options.B: Severe dehydration from vomiting
options.C: Sudden failure of the thyroid gland
options.D: Massive, rapid destruction of cancer cells releasing their contents into the blood

explanation: When chemo works *too* fast, millions of cancer cells burst open at once, spilling their insides (like potassium and uric acid) straight into the bloodstream.

question: When a country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grows, what does it usually mean for the government?

options.A: Lower prices for imported medical equipment
options.B: An immediate end to all infectious diseases
options.C: Free medical training for every citizen
options.D: More revenue to allocate toward public health budgets

explanation: A growing economy brings in more revenue, which gives the government more muscle to fund health services and hospitals.

question: What is the immediate sign that you have accidentally hit the sciatic nerve during a gluteal injection?

options.A: Sharp, burning pain shooting down the patient's leg
options.B: Instant swelling and bright red blood spurting out
options.C: A loud popping sound coming from the hip joint
options.D: The syringe plunger becoming completely jammed

explanation: Spot on. Hitting the sciatic nerve causes an electric, burning shock down the leg. If this happens, stop and withdraw immediately!

question: What is a fecal impaction?

options.A: A hard mass of stool stuck in the rectum
options.B: An infection of the large intestine lining
options.C: The complete absence of bowel sounds
options.D: A tear in the external anal sphincter

explanation: Fecal impaction happens when dried stool collects and packs tightly in the rectum, blocking normal passage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why do doctors still check cervical polyps even though they are usually harmless?

options.A: To stop chronic pelvic pain
options.B: To prevent permanent infertility
options.C: To rule out potential malignancy
options.D: To cure underlying bacterial infections

explanation: Even though most polyps are completely harmless, doctors always check them just to be 100% sure there are no hidden cancer cells. Better safe than sorry!

question: What is the main cause of communicable (spreadable) diseases?

options.A: Genetically inherited cellular mutations
options.B: Nutritional deficiencies in the diet
options.C: Long-term exposure to industrial chemicals
options.D: Infectious agents like bacteria and viruses

explanation: You nailed it! Communicable diseases are caused by tiny living germs like bacteria and viruses that can pass from one person to another.

question: What is a major clinical benefit of Long-Acting Reversible Contraception (LARC) for teenagers?

options.A: They provide permanent sterilization after five years
options.B: They can be inserted independently by the user at home
options.C: They eliminate all risks of contracting viral STIs
options.D: They do not require daily compliance to remain effective

explanation: Once a LARC is placed by a clinician, it works quietly in the background for years without daily effort from the client.

question: Why do nursing schools carry out educational evaluations?

options.A: To check if students are meeting their learning goals
options.B: To rank who is the best or worst in class
options.C: To punish students who struggle in the clinic
options.D: To replace daily attendance registers

explanation: Evaluation isn't about punishment or just ranking you—it's simply a way to check if you're grasping what you need to know to become a great nurse!

question: Why does secondary adrenal hypofunction usually leave aldosterone production alone?

options.A: Aldosterone is primarily regulated by the renin-angiotensin system, not pituitary ACTH.
options.B: The pituitary gland does not influence any part of the adrenal cortex.
options.C: The adrenal medulla takes over aldosterone production when the pituitary fails.
options.D: Aldosterone is produced in a separate organ outside the adrenal glands.

explanation: Remember that aldosterone answers mostly to your kidneys and blood pressure (via the renin-angiotensin system), not the brain's pituitary gland. So if the pituitary slows down, aldosterone often keeps right on working!

question: A nurse cares for a patient with a drug-resistant wound infection. Which principle guides safe nursing care?

options.A: Treating all patient blood and body fluids as infectious using standard precautions
options.B: Reusing medical equipment between patients if it looks visually clean
options.C: Stopping all hand hygiene once gloves are removed from the hands
options.D: Assuming infection control is only necessary if the patient shows a high fever

explanation: Standard precautions require treating all bodily fluids as potentially infectious to protect against both known and unknown pathogens. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h8)

question: A healthy term baby develops mild yellow skin on day three of life, which gradually disappears by day ten without treatment. How is this classified?

options.A: Kernicterus syndrome
options.B: Pathological hemolysis
options.C: Physiological jaundice
options.D: Bile duct obstruction

explanation: Jaundice that appears after 24 hours, peaks early, and resolves on its own within two weeks in a healthy infant is normal physiological jaundice. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h3)

question: Which of these is a must-share piece of information during a patient handover?

options.A: The brand name of the hospital bed mattress
options.B: The patient's favorite television program
options.C: The personal phone number of the patient's relative
options.D: Current vital signs and recent lab results

explanation: Vitals and lab values give a clear, quick picture of how stable the patient is right now.

question: What does a fasting blood sugar test primarily measure?

options.A: Baseline blood glucose after food restriction
options.B: Maximum blood glucose right after a heavy meal
options.C: Average blood sugar over the last three months
options.D: Total amount of insulin stored in the pancreas

explanation: The test measures glucose levels when the body has not consumed calories for several hours, showing the true resting baseline. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h1)

question: What is the purpose of establishing clear inclusion and exclusion criteria?

options.A: To make sure only wealthy patients get selected for trials
options.B: To reduce the total number of hospital beds available
options.C: To prevent doctors from reading the research proposal
options.D: To define precisely who can and cannot safely participate in the study

explanation: Criteria protect patient safety and ensure the studied group matches the exact research question. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which type of depression tends to happen during specific times of the year, especially the cold winter months?

options.A: Seasonal affective disorder
options.B: Postpartum depression
options.C: Major depressive disorder
options.D: Persistent depressive disorder

explanation: You got it! Seasonal affective disorder (SAD) kicks in during certain seasons, usually when daylight gets shorter in the winter.

question: A patient with type 2 diabetes needs help managing their meals. What is a great, simple tip to share first?

options.A: Replace all water intake with fresh vegetable juices only
options.B: Cook your vegetables without any seasoning or oil whatsoever
options.C: Stop eating all forms of food for two days of the week
options.D: Fill half of your meal plate with non-starchy, colorful vegetables

explanation: You nailed it! The plate method is a fantastic, visual way to help patients control portions and get enough fiber without stressful calorie counting.

question: Why can cultural stigma surrounding dementia make things especially tough for families in Nigeria?

options.A: It guarantees that traditional healers will cure the underlying brain damage
options.B: It forces the government to provide free nursing homes in every state
options.C: It eliminates all forms of physical illness in elderly community members
options.D: It can cause families to hide the affected relative and isolate themselves from support

explanation: Stigma creates shame and secrecy, which stops families from reaching out for the healthcare advice and community support they need.

question: Which layer of the skin acts as the main shield blocking most drugs from easily entering the body?

options.A: Stratum corneum
options.B: Sweat gland ducts
options.C: Dermal blood vessels
options.D: Subcutaneous fat layer

explanation: The stratum corneum is the tough outer layer of your epidermis that naturally keeps foreign substances out. Great job remembering your anatomy!

question: Which metabolic process involves building complex body tissues from simpler substances?

options.A: Excretion
options.B: Catabolism
options.C: Anabolism
options.D: Digestion

explanation: Think of 'Anabolism' as adding blocks to build things up—like turning simple amino acids into strong muscles.

question: What is a major use for 5-HT3 receptor antagonists like ondansetron?

options.A: Bacterial gastroenteritis
options.B: Chronic hypertension
options.C: Parkinson's disease tremors
options.D: Chemotherapy-induced nausea

explanation: That's right! Drugs like ondansetron are lifesavers for preventing and treating the heavy nausea caused by cancer treatments and surgeries. You're mastering pharmacology!

question: What is a common downside when a health system relies too heavily on disease-specific vertical programs?

options.A: Basic primary care and non-communicable diseases may be neglected
options.B: Hospitals completely stop admitting patients with surgical emergencies
options.C: Local nurses refuse to administer any form of preventative vaccination
options.D: Infection rates for malaria and HIV instantly rise to record highs

explanation: When international donors laser-focus only on specific epidemics, everyday clinic services and chronic illnesses often get left behind without proper funding.

question: Which primary brain swelling (vesicle) grows into the cerebrum?

options.A: Prosencephalon
options.B: Mesencephalon
options.C: Rhombencephalon
options.D: Myelencephalon

explanation: Well done! The prosencephalon, or forebrain, gives rise to parts that ultimately form our large cerebrum.

question: Which of the following is the best example of clear, objective documentation for a joint assessment?

options.A: Extremities look fine and the patient feels much better today
options.B: Joint is completely normal with standard daily functioning
options.C: Left shoulder active range of motion is 160 degrees with no pain reported
options.D: Patient is lazy and refuses to move their painful arm

explanation: Objective documentation uses measurable data, specific angles, and clear facts rather than subjective opinions. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h9)

question: A nurse notices that the cleaning staff plugged an electric kettle into the same socket used for the vaccine refrigerator. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Leave both plugged in as long as the electricity is stable
options.B: Unplug the kettle and ensure the refrigerator has a dedicated socket
options.C: Move the kettle to another room only when patients are present
options.D: Switch off the refrigerator while the kettle is boiling water

explanation: Vaccine refrigerators must always have a dedicated power source to prevent accidental tripping or power overloads. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h3)

question: Why is cold therapy (ice) applied during the first 24 to 48 hours following an acute soft tissue injury?

options.A: It increases blood flow to warm up the injured muscle
options.B: It causes vasoconstriction to reduce local swelling and pain
options.C: It forces white blood cells to leave the body entirely
options.D: It stimulates scar tissue to form much faster

explanation: Cold constricts local blood vessels, decreasing the amount of fluid that leaks into the surrounding injured tissue. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h7)

question: A nurse is teaching mothers about ORS preparation. Instead of just lecturing, she asks a mother to come forward and mix the solution herself. Which learning principle is the nurse using?

options.A: Strict isolation
options.B: Punitive correction
options.C: Passive observation
options.D: Active participation

explanation: Having the learner perform the task herself ensures she understands the steps through hands-on practice rather than just listening. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of leadership in community health practice?

options.A: Empowering communities to manage their own health
options.B: Reducing the operational costs of local clinics
options.C: Enforcing strict compliance with national hospital policies
options.D: Directing all medical treatment decisions without input

explanation: Community leadership focuses on working alongside the population so they can eventually direct and sustain their own health improvements. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T2#GNS124_U2_T2_h1)

question: What is a major risk factor for developing postpartum depression?

options.A: Experiencing normal first-trimester ambivalence
options.B: Feeling quickening movements in the second trimester
options.C: Attending routine antenatal education classes
options.D: Untreated anxiety or depression during pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! Catching and treating mental health struggles early during pregnancy helps protect the mother after delivery as well.

question: How does chronic disease monitoring by a home health nurse help the patient?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will never experience another symptom
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future physician check-ups
options.C: It catches early warning signs of decline to prevent hospitalization
options.D: It cures long-term illnesses through regular observation alone

explanation: Closely tracking chronic symptoms helps nurses spot worsening health early so they can intervene before an emergency hospital admission is needed. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of the Sex Offender Register created under the VAPP Act?

options.A: To track convicted abusers and prevent them from working in sensitive areas
options.B: To grant tax exemptions to registered citizens
options.C: To help couples find compatible marriage partners
options.D: To provide employment opportunities for convicted individuals

explanation: Correct! The register keeps track of convicted offenders to safeguard vulnerable populations, especially in schools and hospitals.

question: A 15-year-old visits the clinic with eye strain, a stiff neck, and poor sleep after spending 6 hours on social media every night. What is the best term for this?

options.A: Acute digital poisoning from screen radiation
options.B: Computer vision syndrome and lifestyle-related strain
options.C: Congenital sleep apnea triggered by texting
options.D: Muscular dystrophy caused by Wi-Fi signals

explanation: Too much screen time takes a physical toll! It causes tired eyes, bad posture leading to neck pain, and messed-up sleep schedules.

question: A community elder tells you that pregnant women must not eat fish. What is your best initial nursing action?

options.A: Threaten to withdraw primary healthcare services from the entire village
options.B: Publicly announce that the elder is ignorant and should be ignored
options.C: Respectfully listen and discuss the nutritional benefits of fish using local examples
options.D: Give the pregnant woman hidden supplements without telling her family

explanation: Respectful dialogue always wins. It addresses misconceptions without alienating the community leaders who hold influence.

question: What is the main protective antibody packed inside colostrum?

options.A: Immunoglobulin E
options.B: Immunoglobulin A
options.C: Immunoglobulin D
options.D: Immunoglobulin G

explanation: Brilliant! Secretory IgA lines the baby's tummy and intestines, giving them a strong shield against germs.

question: Why might a wonder drug that wins lab awards perform poorly in a rural community?

options.A: Patients may struggle with storage requirements or fail to complete the full dosage course
options.B: Doctors prefer writing paper prescriptions instead of using electronic records
options.C: Hospital administrators charge patients identical fees regardless of income
options.D: The government refuses to tax pharmaceutical companies that import the drug

explanation: Real life has challenges! If a drug needs a fridge or a strict 7-day routine, everyday barriers can lower its real-world success.

question: You are teaching a client with heart failure how to avoid fluid buildup at home. What is the best advice to give?

options.A: Go to the emergency room every time you feel slightly tired
options.B: Stop taking your water pills whenever you feel thirsty
options.C: Drink extra water throughout the day to flush out toxins
options.D: Weigh yourself every morning at the same time and report sudden gains

explanation: You nailed it! Daily morning weights are a quick and reliable way to spot early fluid retention before it becomes dangerous.

question: A researcher targets prisoners for a risky drug trial just because they are locked up and easy to reach. Which ethical rule is being broken?

options.A: Veracity
options.B: Justice
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Beneficence

explanation: Spot on! Justice means fair selection, so vulnerable groups aren't unfairly dumped with all the riskiest studies.

question: A patient with a severe drug overdose has lost consciousness and normal gag reflexes. Why is intubation urgently required here?

options.A: To protect the lungs from choking on stomach contents
options.B: To reverse the chemical effects of the drug quickly
options.C: To increase blood flow to the brain tissue
options.D: To lower the patient's elevated body temperature

explanation: Unconscious patients lose protective airway reflexes, putting them at high risk of aspirating vomit into their lungs, which intubation prevents. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h1)

question: How do unsterile injection techniques lead to painful abscesses?

options.A: By introducing bacteria from the skin surface deep into the muscle tissue
options.B: By causing an immediate chemical reaction that dissolves bone tissue
options.C: By increasing the local blood flow until the tissue swells and bursts
options.D: By freezing the surrounding muscle fibers and destroying blood vessels

explanation: When germs are pushed past the skin into warm muscle, they multiply, cause inflammation, and form pus (an abscess). Good antisepsis stops this!

question: What dangerous illness is linked closely to improperly canned low-acid foods?

options.A: Malaria
options.B: Tuberculosis
options.C: Botulism
options.D: Cholera

explanation: Poor canning can create an airtight space where the germ *Clostridium botulinum* loves to grow and make a dangerous, paralyzing toxin.

question: Which of these is a great example of working with another sector to stop the spread of infections like cholera?

options.A: Hospital pharmacists reviewing drug expiration dates in the dispensary
options.B: Doctors prescribing antibiotics in a private clinic setting
options.C: A head nurse holding a closed meeting with junior nursing students
options.D: Working with public works to ensure clean water supply to prevent cholera

explanation: Spot on! Teaming up with public works to fix water infrastructure stops waterborne diseases right at the source.

question: What does the term 'reduction' mean in the management of fractures?

options.A: Gradual shrinking of local soft tissue swelling using ice packs
options.B: Lowering the patient's blood pressure prior to orthopedic surgery
options.C: Surgical removal of dead bone tissue from an infected site
options.D: Realignment of the broken bone fragments into their normal position

explanation: Reduction is the process of putting displaced bone ends back into their correct anatomical alignment so they can heal properly. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a good public health strategy for controlling parasite infections?

options.A: Treating community populations with deworming drugs
options.B: Promoting open-air defecation near water sources
options.C: Ensuring access to safe and clean drinking water
options.D: Improving sanitation infrastructure and sewage systems

explanation: Open-air defecation near water sources actually spreads parasite eggs and worsens outbreaks—definitely a practice we want to stop! You got this.

question: You are managing a home birth, and the placenta won't come out after 45 minutes even with active management, while bleeding increases. What should you do?

options.A: Encourage the mother to stand up and walk around the room
options.B: Attempt manual removal of the placenta immediately using bare hands
options.C: Wait another hour because retained placenta is completely harmless
options.D: Initiate emergency transfer to a hospital while monitoring bleeding and vital signs

explanation: You made the right call. A retained placenta with extra bleeding is an emergency that needs quick hospital transfer to keep the mother safe.

question: What does human factors engineering mainly look at in a hospital setting?

options.A: The psychological mental health disorders of incoming hospital patients
options.B: How humans interact with equipment, tools, and working environments
options.C: The financial cost of hiring nursing staff for night shift duties
options.D: How physical exercise improves the cardiovascular health of nurses

explanation: Human factors look at how well our tools and workspaces fit our daily tasks, helping us design environments where mistakes are harder to make.

question: How does empowering a patient with a physical disability help them through community nursing care?

options.A: It encourages the patient to take an active role in their own healthcare decisions
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future medical or nursing supervision
options.C: It guarantees immediate employment and financial independence
options.D: It removes all environmental barriers found within the public transport system

explanation: Empowerment builds self-advocacy so patients lead the conversation about their own health instead of just sitting back. You're becoming an advocate nurse!

question: How does drying (dehydration) primarily preserve food?

options.A: By keeping the food at freezing cold temperatures
options.B: By increasing the internal oxygen levels of the food
options.C: By adding large amounts of chemical preservatives
options.D: By removing the water that microorganisms need to grow

explanation: Think of it this way: germs need water to survive and multiply, just like we do. Take the water away, and they can't grow!

question: Which modern workplace design gives workers dual lines of authority where they report to two different managers?

options.A: Simple structure
options.B: Divisional structure
options.C: Matrix structure
options.D: Functional structure

explanation: In a matrix structure, you might report to both your regular department head and a special project manager. It's like having two bosses!

question: In which year was the historic Alma-Ata Declaration on Primary Health Care held?
explanation: The landmark international conference that shaped modern community nursing took place in Alma-Ata in 1978. Great to keep in mind for your exams!

question: A hospitalized patient with chronic bronchitis is struggling to breathe and their oxygen is dropping. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.A: Elevate the head of the bed and assess breathing status
options.B: Wait for the environmental agency to clear the outdoor air
options.C: Discharge the patient immediately so they can get fresh air
options.D: Encourage the patient to perform heavy physical exercise

explanation: Spot on! Always start by positioning the patient to help them breathe better and checking their status before jumping to other steps.

question: What is the main job of mifepristone during a medical abortion?

options.A: Stimulating strong uterine contractions
options.B: Inducing systemic maternal hypertension
options.C: Blocking progesterone receptors to detach the sac
options.D: Paralyzing the musculature of the cervix

explanation: You've got this! Mifepristone blocks progesterone, the hormone needed to maintain pregnancy. This causes the uterine lining to soften and detaches the sac, preparing the way for the next step.

question: What is the primary function of the male reproductive system?

options.A: Filter waste products from the blood
options.B: Produce, sustain, and transport sperm
options.C: Digest complex dietary proteins
options.D: Regulate total body water balance

explanation: The primary role of the male reproductive system is the creation and delivery of sperm cells for reproduction alongside hormone production. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which situation is an example of cross-contamination from poor glove habits?

options.A: Not wearing gloves to take a pulse on an arm
options.B: Touching a computer keyboard with gloves you wore during wound care
options.C: Washing your hands right after taking off both gloves
options.D: Choosing a larger glove size to avoid thumb tears

explanation: Using dirty gloves on shared equipment like keyboards transfers patient germs to surfaces where other staff can pick them up.

question: Why is folic acid so important before and during early pregnancy?

options.A: To prevent neural tube defects
options.B: To strengthen the mother's bones
options.C: To lower maternal blood pressure
options.D: To stop excessive morning sickness

explanation: Brilliant! Folic acid is a true lifesaver in early pregnancy, helping the baby's brain and spine form properly.

question: Why is asking a patient about their recent travel and where they live so important during a nursing assessment?

options.A: It proves whether the patient paid their hospital registration bills
options.B: It determines the patient's exact health insurance coverage tier
options.C: It helps identify exposure to specific infectious disease outbreaks
options.D: It replaces the need for standard laboratory diagnostic tests

explanation: Great thinking! Knowing where a patient has been helps link their current symptoms to ongoing disease outbreaks in those areas.

question: Which term covers both undernutrition and overnutrition?

options.A: Homeostasis
options.B: Anabolism
options.C: Metabolism
options.D: Malnutrition

explanation: Malnutrition isn't just about not having enough food—it's an umbrella term for any poor nutrition, whether someone is eating too little or too much.

question: What is the main reason for holding community disaster drills?

options.A: To replace the need for written emergency preparedness guides
options.B: To help residents turn emergency knowledge into practical muscle memory
options.C: To punish people who fail to follow local sanitation laws
options.D: To test the physical strength of professional rescue workers

explanation: You're doing great! Drills give people practice so they can react quickly and calmly when a real emergency strikes.

question: A patient in a disaster zone has a severe head injury, is unresponsive, breathing irregularly, and has no pulse. Which triage category fits best?

options.A: Red
options.B: Black
options.C: Yellow
options.D: Green

explanation: You're doing great. A black tag (or expectant) is used for catastrophic injuries where survival is sadly very unlikely, helping us save resources for those we can help.

question: Why is drawing a community map so useful for health planning?

options.A: It guarantees financial grants from international donor agencies
options.B: It provides exact genetic profiles of every newborn in the ward
options.C: It replaces the need for nurses to ever visit the village physically
options.D: It reveals geographical inequalities and the physical location of health hazards

explanation: Brilliant! Mapping shows you where resources and environmental dangers are located, helping you reach isolated spots.

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine separates exposed healthy people
options.B: Isolation is for bacterial infections, while quarantine is for viral diseases
options.C: Quarantine lasts for one year, while isolation lasts for only two hours
options.D: Quarantine is done in a hospital, while isolation is always done in a market

explanation: Easy way to remember: Isolation is for those who are already sick, while quarantine is for healthy people who were exposed and need to wait out the incubation period.

question: How can you tell the difference between the baby's side of the placenta and the mother's side?

options.A: The fetal surface contains the placental cotyledons, while the maternal surface has the umbilical cord insertion.
options.B: The fetal surface is smooth, shiny, and shows branching blood vessels, while the maternal surface is rough and divided into cotyledons.
options.C: The fetal surface is dark red and rough, while the maternal surface is covered by a clear, slippery amniotic membrane.
options.D: There is no visual difference between the two sides of a mature human placenta.

explanation: Picture it this way: the baby's side faces the shiny amniotic sac with visible blood vessels, while the mother's side faces the uterine wall and looks bumpy and rough.

question: Why is building trust through compassionate nursing care important in reproductive health?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will never experience complications
options.B: It encourages clients to seek timely medical attention
options.C: It allows nurses to skip standard physical assessments
options.D: It eliminates the need for any medical documentation

explanation: You got it! When clients trust us as nurses, they feel safe and are much more likely to visit the clinic early for antenatal care and family planning.

question: Why must nurses and doctors look at age and kidney function along with genetic test results?

options.A: Liver and kidney function change every few minutes in healthy adults
options.B: Non-genetic factors also significantly influence drug metabolism and clearance
options.C: Genetic variations only matter during the initial absorption phase
options.D: Genetic tests are notoriously inaccurate and cannot be trusted alone

explanation: Exactly! Genes are super important, but things like your age, overall health, and how well your organs are working also change how your body handles medicine. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T5#GNS125_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the main goal of Nigeria's National Reproductive Health Policy and Strategic Framework?

options.A: To reduce high rates of maternal and child mortality
options.B: To replace traditional birth attendants with medical doctors
options.C: To privatize all primary health care centers in the country
options.D: To increase the importation of foreign pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: You've got this! The core aim of this framework is to tackle the heavy burden of maternal and child deaths through coordinated health actions.

question: Which of the following is a major limitation of non-experimental research?

options.A: Excessive control over the natural hospital environment
options.B: Impossibility of using statistical analysis
options.C: Unethical manipulation of patient treatment plans
options.D: Inability to definitively establish cause and effect

explanation: Great thinking! Because we aren't controlling every single outside factor or changing variables on purpose, we can't say for sure that one thing caused another.

question: A client started birth control pills two weeks ago and comes back worried about mild, irregular spotting. What should you do first as her nurse?

options.A: Prescribe a high-dose antibiotic to treat a presumed uterine infection
options.B: Refer her urgently to a surgeon for an exploratory pelvic examination
options.C: Advise her to stop taking the medication immediately and switch to surgical sterilization
options.D: Reassure her that irregular spotting is normal during the first few months of adjustment

explanation: Spot on! Early spotting is very common when the body is getting used to new hormones. A little reassurance goes a long way while her body adjusts.

question: What post-procedure instruction should a nurse give to a patient who just received a knee injection?

options.A: Remove the sterile bandage right away and soak in mud
options.B: Run a long distance immediately to spread the medicine
options.C: Take off all clothes and stay in a hot sauna for hours
options.D: Rest the joint and apply ice packs to reduce swelling

explanation: Resting the joint and icing it helps prevent excess irritation and controls post-injection discomfort. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h7)

question: Which level of prevention stops risk factors from even starting through broad social and economic policies?

options.A: Clinical rehabilitation
options.B: Secondary prevention
options.C: Primordial prevention
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: Primordial prevention is all about stopping risk factors before they even take root in a society through broad policies.

question: Which of these medications is considered a minor tranquilizer?

options.A: Chlorpromazine
options.B: Risperidone
options.C: Diazepam
options.D: Haloperidol

explanation: Diazepam is a benzodiazepine, which doctors commonly use as a minor tranquilizer to help calm anxiety. Great practice for your pharmacology exams!

question: Why is it super helpful for nurses to understand basic X-ray imaging?

options.A: To replace the radiologist in reading films
options.B: To prescribe the correct radiation dosage
options.C: To operate the heavy X-ray machine safely
options.D: To help coordinate care and ease patient anxiety

explanation: As a nurse, you are the friendly face who prepares patients and calms their nerves before procedures. Great nursing starts with great communication!

question: How does a rehab facility differ from a regular acute care hospital ward?

options.A: Rehab facilities deal strictly with infectious diseases, while acute care wards handle surgeries.
options.B: Rehab facilities prohibit family visitation to protect the therapy schedule.
options.C: Acute care hospitals do not employ registered nurses, whereas rehab facilities are nurse-run.
options.D: Acute care focuses on life-saving stabilization, while rehab focuses on restoring functional independence.

explanation: Spot on! Acute care handles the active crisis, while rehab steps in once the patient is stable enough to focus on long-term recovery and therapy.

question: In medical storage, what does the FEFO rule stand for?

options.A: First-Expired, First-Out
options.B: Fast-Entry, Fast-Output
options.C: Forward-Examination, Final-Order
options.D: First-Evaluated, Freight-Out

explanation: You nailed it! FEFO means items closest to their expiry date get used first so nothing goes to waste.

question: How is an adverse drug reaction (ADR) different from a normal side effect?

options.A: An ADR is typically harmful and unexpected at normal doses
options.B: An ADR only happens when a patient overdoses on medication
options.C: Side effects cannot be anticipated by healthcare providers
options.D: Side effects are always dangerous while ADRs are harmless

explanation: Side effects are often expected mild reactions, but an ADR is an unwanted, harmful response that happens even when the drug is taken correctly at normal doses.

question: Which item belongs inside the yellow infectious waste bin during an immunization session?

options.A: Food wrappers left over from the outreach lunch break
options.B: Cardboard packaging boxes that held the vaccine vials
options.C: Cotton swabs stained with blood or vaccine fluid
options.D: Empty plastic water bottles brought by clinic staff

explanation: Items contaminated with body fluids or biological residues must go into biohazard infectious bins to prevent contamination. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h6)

question: Which health model looks at wellness strictly as having no physical signs or symptoms of sickness?

options.A: Role performance model
options.B: Clinical model
options.C: Adaptive model
options.D: Eudaimonistic model

explanation: You've got this! The clinical model is the classic medical approach: if nothing hurts and you have no visible sickness, you are healthy.

question: A patient had surgery on their knee joint two days ago. When should the nurse expect these sutures to be removed?

options.A: In 30 days minimum
options.B: In 14 days or more
options.C: In 7 to 8 days
options.D: In 3 to 5 days

explanation: Joint areas experience constant pulling and stretching, requiring a longer healing time and delayed suture removal to prevent reopening. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h2)

question: Why is post-natal care just as crucial as the care a mother gets during pregnancy?

options.A: Many serious health complications happen during the weeks after delivery.
options.B: The baby no longer needs any medical attention after birth.
options.C: Hormones return to normal instantly without any professional help.
options.D: It gives the mother time to rest away from her family members.

explanation: Spotting issues early saves lives! A large percentage of maternal and newborn complications happen right after birth, which is why close monitoring during the post-natal phase is a total lifesaver.

question: Which of these actions is WRONG when monitoring a client's nutritional progress?

options.A: Checking regular weight trends over time
options.B: Ignoring client feedback on food preferences
options.C: Documenting specific physical measurements
options.D: Reviewing the client's recent food diaries

explanation: Never ignore what the client likes! Diet plans only work if they fit the client's personal lifestyle and taste.

question: Who was a key pioneer of the Moral Treatment movement in France?

options.A: Sigmund Freud
options.B: Dorothea Dix
options.C: Florence Nightingale
options.D: Philippe Pinel

explanation: Philippe Pinel famously ordered the chains removed from patients in Paris asylums and introduced humane treatment. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why must a gravity drainage bag always be positioned below the level of the wound?

options.A: To use gravity to pull fluid out and prevent it from flowing back
options.B: To make it easier for the patient to walk around the unit
options.C: To keep the collection bag hidden from the patient's direct view
options.D: To stop the tubing from becoming permanently kinked or twisted

explanation: If the collection container is higher than the wound, fluid inside the tubing can flow backward into the body cavity, introducing bacteria and causing infection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h2)

question: How do measurable metrics help a nurse manager evaluate a ward plan?

options.A: They provide concrete data to show whether the unit met its targets.
options.B: They eliminate the need for annual performance appraisals.
options.C: They allow the manager to guess how hard the staff worked.
